title: Majestic Collab: Bring the Knight Back
summary: Capture both rooks and the queen with checking knight moves, then return the knight to control the escape square before pawn mate.

nodes.question: What must the knight do after it wins all the major pieces?
nodes.explanation: Nxd5+, Nxe7+ and Nxg8+ remove both rooks and the queen with check. White must then return through e7 to d5, controlling f4 when g3 advances to g4 mate.

branches.title: Source finish: capture, return, then pawn mate
commentary: Begin after ...Kf6 with all eleven pieces present. The earlier sacrifices are context; this lesson verifies the final checking sweep and return route.
Nxd5+ captures the rook on d5 while checking f6. White keeps the king under attack rather than giving the queen time to act.
Kf5 is the sole legal reply. Black’s own e5 pawn and e6 knight, together with Kh6 and White’s pawns, restrict the king.
Nxe7+ captures the second rook with check. The knight on e7 attacks f5 while the queen on g8 remains available for the next fork.
Kf6 is the sole legal reply. The king steps onto a square attacked when the knight captures on g8.
Nxg8+ takes the queen with check against f6. White has removed all three major pieces, but the mating plan still needs the knight in the right place.
Kf5 is the sole legal reply. Pushing g4 now would vacate f4, allowing the king to escape there.
Ne7+ starts the return route with another check. The knight does not stay on the square where it won the queen.
Kf6 is again forced. The king continues to oscillate between the squares dictated by the knight checks.
Nd5+ returns to the central square, checking f6 and controlling f4. This restores the coverage that g3 will stop providing when it advances.
Kf5 is the sole legal reply. Every Black reply in the saved tree has been checked; none of the apparent king flights is available.
g4# checks f5. Nd5 covers f4 and f6, f3 controls e4 and protects g4, Kh6 controls g5/g6, and Black’s own Ne6 and e5 pawn block e6/e5. The knight’s return makes the pawn advance mate.
branches.explanation: g4# checks f5. Nd5 covers f4 and f6, f3 controls e4 and protects g4, Kh6 controls g5/g6, and Black’s own Ne6 and e5 pawn block e6/e5. The knight’s return makes the pawn advance mate.

exercises.prompt: Why not push g4 immediately after taking the queen?
exercises.answer: Moving the g3 pawn gives up its control of f4. The knight on g8 does not cover f4, so Kf4 is legal after an early g4+.

exercises.prompt: Why return to d5 after winning the queen?
exercises.answer: Nd5 controls f4 as well as f6. It replaces the g3 pawn’s guard of f4 before the pawn advances with mate.
